approach.method_basis: The Parent generates new molecular graphs by mutation and crossover, learns from accepted session scores, and selects sequential sampled maxima. A count-fingerprint Gaussian process supplies the mean, stalled-pool eligibility and correlated latent draws. An eight-view native quantile model retains all fingerprint columns, including centered query values at coordinates constant in training. Its sorted quantile curve is linear between knots, constant beyond the endpoint knots, and translated by its integrated mean to the GP location before selecting purchases.
approach.novelty: Complete the two constant endpoint tails with the source exponential law, then recenter the completed distribution to the same GP mean. This adds continuous support beyond the endpoint knots while preserving their interior spacings and the original correlated draws. Unlike siblings that substituted Gaussian shape, transported GP amplitude, zeroed query-only inputs or removed dependence, this changes only the omitted tail completion and its necessary mean correction. The test asks whether that completion changes paid exploration enough to improve full gain over the actual generating parents.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-ada68e100737 uses constant tails outside its 999 native knots. The frozen Search-policy review measures 401/4350 paid outcomes below the active GP-shifted .001 endpoint (0.09218390804597701) and 77/4350 above .999 (0.017701149425287357); central 90% coverage is 0.7735632183908046 and mean 999-grid pinball 0.02057102996383421. This is missing predictive support, not proof that added support improves search. Parent execution is complete: all fifteen endpoints, macro 0.5622564516615843 and seed population SD 0.005481732549278124; full/late generating-parent positive gain is 16.68612674725103/3.915646383849673. Its own-Parent delta is +0.0032675763122120096, but formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de deficit is -0.04477386454954668 and published task_safe is false. Source inspection confirms the full-width input and exact GP-location capabilities inherited from n-e2506e11f536. n-cfd49808a894 GP-amplitude and n-741da1149559 Gaussian-shape transfers refuted their full-and-late predictions despite complete execution; neither tested source exponential completion. n-cfa00d1cee11 supports retained nonzero-C only under its scoped removal. n-a511fe4e5301 has 14/15 endpoints and incomplete feedback, so its dependence contribution remains unresolved.

hypothesis: Source-native exponential tail completion of the conditional quantile marginal, with analytic own-law mean recentering and the existing GP Gaussian copula. With a=.001, sorted q_j at p_j=j/1000, estimate beta_L from OLS of first 20 q_j on log(p_j), and beta_R from negative OLS slope of last 20 q_j on log(1-p_j); use source abs then clip each scale to [.01,100]. Define Q_L(p)=q_L+beta_L*log(p/a) below a and Q_R(p)=q_R-beta_R*log((1-p)/a) above 1-a; retain the original piecewise-linear interior. Let m_exp be the exact integral of this completed curve. Consume S_i=mu_GP_i+Q_exp_i(Phi(z_i))-m_exp_i with the unchanged z=(Z@F.T)/sqrt(row_sum(F^2)). Positive finite scales remove endpoint atoms and permit tail-sensitive sampled choices; completing and translating the curve may thereby change paid offspring and full actual-generating-parent gain. The only downstream directional prediction is full gain >16.68612674725103 on complete exposed execution. Late gain, calibration and endpoints remain separate.

finding_summary.headline: Tail completion changed paid choices, but full generating-parent gain fell despite a stronger late half
finding_summary.insights:
Restoring support removes the artificial endpoint atoms and reaches actual purchases, but it did not make the complete search more productive under the registered test. The loss is concentrated earlier: gain in the first 100 purchases per session fell from 7.90446 to 6.55561, while late gains rose. This rules out absent tail exposure or broken feedback as explanations for the failed full-gain prediction. It also separates proper scoring from search utility: a small CRPS benefit and more parent-beating events coexist with less total improvement over actual parents. Because the completed curve must be recentered, 2,187 paid predictions also receive a nonzero interior shift; this experiment prices that joint change and cannot attribute the outcome to extrapolation alone. The borrowed endpoint regressions, continuous tails and analytic moments operated; GP recentering and unclipped log-tail evaluation remain adaptations of the source regression method.

The trajectory still spends much of its budget on refinements that do not improve their actual parents: 3,625 of 4,350 purchases give zero positive gain, including 210 exact parent-score ties, and only 14 of the 117 active-only purchases become parents of a later paid descendant. The Molecular assessment describes broad ring-graph variation but recurring favorable chemical families, more very large molecules (518 versus 367 with at least 50 heavy atoms), unusual nitrogen-halogen connectivity and unresolved stereochemistry. This supports a limitation in producing and ranking chemically coherent alternatives, rather than treating graph novelty or tail support as useful exploration by itself. A different graph proposal operator or predictive ranking model could address that class of limitation; these data do not establish which would succeed or that chemical cleanup improves the objective. The result settles this exact full-gain prediction on this host and panel. The broader native-marginal approach, separate tail-versus-recentering contribution, retained components and generalization remain open.
finding_summary.results:
The tail law executed correctly in all 15 sessions. Its 435 allocations used 322 upper-tail selections, changed 165 paid positions and introduced 117 identities outside the same-state constant-tail selected sets. Every one of the 4,350 purchases had a prospective law, accepted score and actual generating-parent join; all 4,200 purchases with a next-fit opportunity entered both real models. The registered primary gain fell from 16.68613 to 15.77071 (−0.91541), so the full-gain prediction is refuted. Nine of fifteen cell gains decreased. The late 2,175 purchases improved from 3.91565 to 5.25064 and the number of parent-beating purchases rose from 697 to 725, but neither replaces the registered full-gain test.

Mean proper CRPS improved only slightly on the identical paid labels, from 0.03548644 for passive constant tails to 0.03548507 for completion. Both laws retained 76.85% central-90% coverage. Endpoint mean fell to 0.542961 from the code Parent’s 0.562256 and remained below the formal Anchor’s 0.607030. The endpoint pairs contain five wins, nine losses and one tie; the largest seed loss is 0.063757. All cells completed, with no technical failure or missing prospective feedback; the Child’s trusted task-safety decision is unavailable.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich molecules span compact amines and oversized heteroaromatics, with recurring N-halogen bonds and unresolved stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of n-79249e04c004 against the issued code Parent n-ada68e100737, limited to frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 and all five tasks. The request distinguishes complete Child evaluation from complete Parent pairing and declares both complete; all 30 issued trajectory files and 6 associated summaries are present, all cell summaries are ok, and all 9,000 initial/proposed rows parse with RDKit. No failure or missing-path cell was dropped. Each node contributes 4,350 accepted optimizer records, separate from its initial observations; these files do not reveal every unpurchased internally generated graph. Both nodes retain 21 proposals of at most 5 heavy atoms; Child has 518 proposals of at least 50 heavy atoms versus Parent 367. This is a broad collection of perceived ring graphs with much narrower favorable chemical families within individual sessions. Child typed/generic Murcko counts, in fixed task order, are 209/131, 482/391, 344/233, 427/265 and 357/171; Parent counts are 210/99, 381/289, 506/381, 409/244 and 343/156. Count differences alone do not prove useful scaffold exploration. Fragment-excluded median maximum Morgan similarity to each session's initial molecules (query and reference each at least 10 heavy atoms) is Child 0.2791, 0.2277, 0.1542, 0.1959, 0.2022 versus Parent 0.3231, 0.2211, 0.1507, 0.2059, 0.2273, rounded from the audit; no reference-target similarity or external library is used. Every task has ring-closure text rate at least 0.9839, consistent with rich rings. Stereocentre text rate is zero throughout; RDKit finds potential tetrahedral centres in 2,193 Child and 1,834 Parent proposals but no specified centres in either. Valid valence and measured scores are not synthesis or activity certification. Chemical associations do not identify which algorithmic component contributed, and this report gives no activation, selection or mechanism verdict. Exact original/copy hashes and future archive mappings are in policy/scratch/r0067-01-improve-L01/molecular/source-audit-final.json. Full row-level descriptors are in the 30 audit-seed files listed there; aggregate methods and results are in policy/scratch/r0067-01-improve-L01/molecular/aggregate-chemistry-audit.json; the documented SMARTS limitation and corrected carbon-centred cumulene audit are in policy/scratch/r0067-01-improve-L01/molecular/supplementary-chemistry-audit.json; every cited Child SMILES/score/evaluation is checked against an original trusted row in policy/scratch/r0067-01-improve-L01/molecular/citation-checks-v1.json. Parent score comparisons use the corresponding issued published trajectories and summaries, all mapped in the source audit.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact, flat indole-like fused heteroaromatics bearing aryl amides or aryl ketones, methyl/alkenyl groups, ethers and frequent halogens. The 870 Child proposals span 3–47 heavy atoms, median 25, with median 3 rings and 3 aromatic rings; Parent median size is 24. Seed 0 ends around a fused heteroaromatic N-halo anilide, seed 1 an indolyl-pyridyl ketone, and seed 2 N-hydroxy anilides with N-sulfur or N-bromine substitution. Ordinary aryl-amide connectivity is recognizable, but several high scorers carry bonds that make isolation and stability questionable. Child typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 209/131 versus Parent 210/99; these are graph counts, not evidence of useful synthetic diversity.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 127/870 Child proposals; N–O single bonds occur in 152/870. N-hydroxy amides are a recognizable functional class, but should not be conflated with the plausibility of N-bromo/N-chloro amides or halogenated ring nitrogens.
Flat aromatic-rich series and repeated local heteroatom/halogen edits dominate the favorable molecules; the occasional very small and enlarged products retain poor scores.
missing_features: The observed favorable compact heteroaromatic/carbonyl architecture is present; the remaining chemical gap is a consistently ordinary, stable realization of that architecture without N-halogen or unusual N-sulfur termination. These rows do not establish that such cleanup would improve the score.

No specified tetrahedral stereochemistry is emitted, including in the 143 Child proposals with RDKit potential centres. No unseen target-specific group requirement can be inferred from this trajectory.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 evaluation-165 N-hydroxy anilide scores 0.4619578459378901; the seed-0 evaluation-254 N-bromo anilide scores 0.4583138045844064. By contrast, COS at seed 0 evaluation 33 scores 7.57511964403052e-19 and the oversized linked indole-amide at seed 1 evaluation 44 scores 3.3811572294260344e-18. Thus the observed gradient favors compact connected aromatic/carbonyl arrangements over either tiny fragments or duplication of that motif; it does not show a general benefit from size growth. Seed-1 evaluation 248 reaches 0.42348216717712805 with a ketone, so amide retention is not an absolute requirement. Child versus Parent best scores in seed order are 0.4583138045844064/0.4387992465191, 0.42348216717712805/0.4033121758994662, and 0.4619578459378901/0.4619578459378901. The last seed-2 molecule is a thioamide/N-fluoro variant at 0.39905049777278273, below its earlier best.

per_task.generated_character: This output is much larger than the other task panels: polyaryl/polyheteroaryl assemblies with fused imide-like dicarbonyl heterocycles, anilino or imine connections, esters, fluoroaryl groups and occasional sulfur carbonyls. Child proposals span 1–120 heavy atoms, median 53.5, with median 8 rings and 7 aromatic rings. Parent medians are 44 heavy atoms and 5 rings. Seed-0 and seed-1 best structures have 75 and 84 heavy atoms respectively, whereas the seed-2 best series is a more recognizable heteroaryl–ester assembly; evaluation 261 has terminal ethynyl and vinyl groups and multiple nitrogen heterocycles. Synthesizing the extended and heavily fused products would be substantially more demanding than their valence-valid SMILES suggest.
liabilities: The Child contains 452/870 proposals with at least 50 heavy atoms versus Parent 303/870, while also retaining 9 very small proposals of at most 5 heavy atoms versus Parent 5. Both tails remain included in the assessment.

Large repeated heteroaromatic units, crowded ring connections, imine/enamine networks and 150 N-halogen-containing proposals raise stability, synthesis and ordinary drug-likeness concerns. A score plateau across N-alkyl and N-bromo variants is not chemical validation.
missing_features: The trajectory demonstrates the rewarded connected aromatic/heteroaromatic content, but does not demonstrate a comparably successful compact, synthetically straightforward representation of all that content. An unseen missing scaffold cannot be deduced from these scores.
Stereochemically specified versions are absent even where bridged or saturated edits introduce potential centres; score benefit from specifying them is unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The tiny fragment FOCl at seed 1 evaluation 223 and C#CC#C at seed 2 evaluation 283 both score 0.5. The extended seed-2 heteroaryl ester at evaluation 261 scores 0.6042729230420492, and the N-brominated final variant at evaluation 300 has exactly the same score. Across within-seed lower/upper score deciles, median heavy-atom count rises from 27 to 77; this is a descriptive size association, not proof that enlargement causes improvement. Child versus Parent seed best scores are 0.5981334841628959/0.608359133126935, 0.6008476307189543/0.5936416783072068 and 0.6042729230420492/0.6324541616056452. The Child has more very large molecules yet no uniformly improved endpoint across seeds. Repeated equal scores for terminal substitutions also give little evidence for their detailed chemical value.

per_task.generated_character: Halogenated aromatic rings and amines dominate. Seed 2 reaches comparatively conventional aryl-substituted tetrahydropyridines with a benzyl-linked tertiary amine, propyl substituents and haloalkyl side chains; seed 0 instead reaches densely bridged polycyclic amines, and seed 1 an unsaturated aryl system bearing an aminomethyl group and alcohol. Child median size is 29 heavy atoms, with 4 rings and 2 aromatic rings; the full size range is 13–110 heavy atoms. Parent medians are 30 heavy atoms and 5 rings. The best seed-2 architecture looks more medicinally familiar than the cage-like seed-0 endpoint, but haloalkyl reactivity and undefined stereochemistry remain unresolved.
liabilities: Alkyl chloride/bromide/iodide SMARTS matches 424/870 Child proposals versus 280/870 Parent proposals; high scores therefore coexist with potentially reactive aliphatic halides.

Dense bridges, congested rings and unresolved stereochemistry compromise the synthetic interpretation of some otherwise high-scoring structures. Nominally neutral SMILES do not establish absence of basicity or the assay-relevant protonation state.
missing_features: Basic-amine-like centres on ring systems are present, so their absence would be a false diagnosis. What is missing is stereochemical specification for the complex ring and side-chain arrangements: 804/870 Child proposals have RDKit potential tetrahedral centres but none specify any.

The favorable amine/aromatic relationship is not consistently realized in comparably simple structures across seeds; the seed-0 high scorer carries 7 perceived rings and an intricate bridged framework. Neither an unseen receptor interaction nor required protonation state is established by these data.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed-2 evaluation 281, the diaryl/tetrahydropyridine tertiary amine, scores 0.9935222927420004, versus 0.00016650955053713697 for the early sulfonylated pyrrolidine/N-chloro amide at evaluation 20. A related phenol at evaluation 264 already scores 0.9848538350578465, so the terminal chloroethyl group is not necessary for a high observed score. The larger low-score decile has median 41 heavy atoms; the high-score decile has 29. The documented nonconjugated-amine SMARTS matches 82/87 upper-decile molecules versus 9/87 lower-decile molecules. This supports an association with accessible amine/aromatic topology, not a claim of affinity or a causal functional-group requirement. Child versus Parent seed best scores are 0.9829418445945004/0.9999974292469022, 0.8082558506474721/0.9845482536896144 and 0.9935222927420004/0.9937212305252073. Final seed-2 evaluation 300 retains the same amine series and scores 0.9683260122919414.

per_task.generated_character: The favorable molecules are aromatic-rich polycycles coupled to nitrogen-containing, carbonyl-bearing larger rings, with propyl/ethoxy substituents and frequent N–N or N–O links. The seed-0 best molecule includes a large ring containing oxygen, carbonyls and adjacent methylated nitrogens; seed 1 gives an extended fused aromatic system with a diaza carbonyl ring; seed 2 favors quinoline-like aromatic material linked through N/O to a nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl ring. Child proposals span 1–73 heavy atoms, median 32, and median 5 rings; the Parent also has median 32 heavy atoms and 5 rings. These are substantial molecular graphs with recognizable fragments, but the combined heteroatom connectivity and larger-ring construction make synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: N–N links occur in 362/870 and N–O links in 216/870 Child proposals, compared with 181/870 and 82/870 in Parent. These flags include recognizable functional classes and are not automatic instability verdicts, but the actual high-scoring macrocyclic combinations merit caution.

Both size tails remain: 11 Child proposals have at most 5 heavy atoms and 25 have at least 50; Parent counts are 15 and 24. Tiny disconnected-from-pharmacophore fragments do not provide useful favorable chemistry merely because they are valid molecules.
missing_features: The trajectories show favorable aromatic/carbonyl combinations but not a clean, consistently higher-scoring realization that avoids unusual adjacent-nitrogen and N–O linkages. No particular unseen target motif is identifiable from these modest scores.
The output lacks stereochemically resolved saturated ring alternatives even though 321 Child proposals contain RDKit potential centres.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-0 evaluation-282 extended N–N/carbonyl ring scores 0.24138596603198878, compared with 0.1678386594791329 for initial evaluation 7, an aryl-linked fused dicarbonyl heterocycle. C#C at seed 2 evaluation 251 and NNO at seed 0 evaluation 29 score 0.0. High-score deciles retain carbonyl-bearing nitrogen chemistry and increase median heavy-atom count modestly from 31 to 34; median aromatic ring count declines from 4 to 3 while carbon saturation increases. Child versus Parent seed best scores are 0.24138596603198878/0.2338424221286825, 0.22696201911046923/0.23322566212666948 and 0.23133958921932535/0.23666901586613867. The Child N–N single-bond presence rises to 362/870 versus Parent 181/870, but the paired seed results are mixed: that enrichment is not evidence that N–N bonding caused a general benefit. Final seed-2 evaluation 300 scores 0.21876186891295196.

per_task.generated_character: The output centers on carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles with fluorine, methyl groups and partially unsaturated ring substituents. Child median size is 27 heavy atoms and 4 rings, matching Parent medians; the Child range is 8–51 heavy atoms. The best seed-2 molecule has 27 heavy atoms and 4 rings but no RDKit aromatic ring: it is a fused dicarbonyl nitrogen system with imine/diene substituent rings, C–F groups, an alcohol and an N–F bond. Seed 0 instead supplies a sulfur-containing fused polycycle with N-fluorination; seed 1 supplies an allene-bearing nitrogen heterocycle. Thus the overall aromatic string rate of 0.7931 does not mean the highest scorer is aromatic.
liabilities: N-halogen bonding appears in 433/870 Child proposals versus 217/870 Parent proposals, and in 75/87 Child upper-decile molecules. This striking enrichment supports a chemistry concern, not a recommendation to pursue N-fluorination.

Carbon-centred cumulated bonds, nonaromatic diene/imine rings and undefined stereochemistry complicate stability and synthesis. The digest cumulated-double-bond string rate is 0.1057; the full graph audit distinguishes carbon-centred cumulenes from ordinary sulfonyl groups.
missing_features: The favored compact fluorinated heterocyclic/carbonyl content is present; the missing demonstrated capability is to realize it consistently with ordinary, isolable connectivity rather than N–F substitution and strained or strongly unsaturated ring editing. The trajectory does not prove that removing these liabilities would raise the objective.
All 584 Child proposals with RDKit potential tetrahedral centres remain stereochemically unspecified; neither a specific enantiomer nor an unseen reference structure is established as the answer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best seed-2 evaluation 285 scores 0.5800842532560502; the related C-fluoromethyl substitution at evaluation 222 scores 0.5639458882746866. The much larger repeated dicarbonyl heterocycle at seed 1 evaluation 83 scores 5.892269813786251e-26. Even late close-looking variants differ sharply: seed-2 evaluation 296 scores 0.003341791417613794, whereas evaluation 299 scores 0.5304745444917758. The visible association favors compact fluorinated nitrogen/carbonyl architectures over duplication, but these multi-edit comparisons cannot isolate fluorine position, saturation or linkage as the cause. Child versus Parent seed best scores are 0.49109529357027587/0.49317199895702235, 0.4418174424064177/0.6054215806683655 and 0.5800842532560502/0.5147249403189217. The final seed-2 imino variant scores 0.2515763774692868.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-79249e04c004, complete frozen Search panel under the issued profile: 2,193/4,350 accepted optimizer molecules have RDKit potential tetrahedral centres, yet none specify one. Parent n-ada68e100737 likewise has 1,834 such molecules with no specified centres. These are graph-perception counts over the exact trajectories, not a claim that stereochemistry is scored or that each assigned isomer would be accessible.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not demonstrate stereochemically resolved output, even for complex saturated or bridged products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need the capability to represent and preserve chemically coherent stereochemistry when it creates such centres. The current evidence identifies an absent output capability; it does not choose an intervention or assert an endpoint benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-79249e04c004 versus n-ada68e100737 under the same complete frozen Search panel: N-halogen SMARTS presence is 754/4,350 versus 719/4,350 proposals. Individual high-scoring molecules retain N–F, N–Br or N–Cl bonds, while other favorable molecules use ordinary carbon-linked amines and amides. Nitrogen–oxygen and nitrogen–nitrogen links also occur; their presence alone does not establish instability.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ordinary functional-group connectivity is not reliably preserved in chemically favorable output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing general capability is reliable access to ordinary, synthetically interpretable realizations of the aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements already generated, with explicit distinction between conventional functional classes and unusual heteroatom–halogen termination. The observed score associations do not establish that removing any alert improves performance, or attribute this limitation to a particular component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-79249e04c004, all 4,350 accepted optimizer records on the frozen Search panel: 21 have at most 5 heavy atoms and 518 have at least 50, compared with 21 and 367 for Parent n-ada68e100737. Favorable molecules include both compact amine/carbonyl architectures and large repeated heteroaromatic assemblies; the direction of the observed size association differs by session, so the pooled counts do not identify a universal optimum.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator spans both tiny fragments and very large repetitive structures without demonstrating consistently useful intermediate-size alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The task-agnostic chemical capability gap is productive control of molecular size while preserving connected functional relationships, including compact alternatives to repeated-unit expansion. These conditions rule out treating a global size cap or a task-specific target scaffold as an established answer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-79249e04c004 and its code Parent n-ada68e100737, complete frozen Search panel: typed and generic Murcko diversity is substantial, but favorable molecules repeatedly share session-local indole/carbonyl, nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl, polyaryl or amine scaffolds. High scores coexist with unusual bonds, crowded bridges and larger rings. Fragment-excluded similarities to the supplied initial set are descriptive only; no matched component intervention establishes chemical mediation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many distinct ring graphs do not demonstrate equally broad, chemically credible high-score solutions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: What remains unshown is broad access to distinct, synthetically plausible arrangements of the useful functional groups, rather than counting graph novelty as chemical coverage. Future use of this gap must retain its source and Search conditions and evaluate any proposed capability without hidden task identity; no scientific intervention is selected here.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
